subject.title: [security] E2B stop deletes sandboxes from metadata without an exact local claim

question: Should E2B stop/delete require an exact local Crabbox claim before deleting any provider sandbox, including raw, synthetic, and cbx metadata fallback identifiers?
rationale: This changes a destructive provider-resource boundary and may affect raw-ID cleanup convenience, so maintainers should confirm the security posture before repair work proceeds.

options.title: Require exact local claim
options.body: Reject claimless E2B deletion targets by default and keep raw/provider metadata lookup for read-only discovery or explicit adoption only.

options.title: Add explicit adoption first
options.body: Keep provider-ID recovery possible only through a deliberate reclaim/adoption flow that persists a fresh exact claim before deletion.

options.title: Keep metadata deletion fallback
options.body: Preserve the current convenience path and accept that provider metadata remains destructive authority for E2B stop.

recommendation.title: Require exact local claim
recommendation.body: Reject claimless E2B deletion targets by default and keep raw/provider metadata lookup for read-only discovery or explicit adoption only.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the current blamed E2B stop/resolver lines and recent adjacent security boundary work, making them the best routing candidate for the decision.
